findings.text: _identity_listing answers from the memoised listing whenever the directory's own entry-set stamp is unchanged, so a sibling rewritten in place keeps its old per-file signature in the listing that _directory_identity_index (:857) revalidates the held index against, the index is reused and _canonical_identity_is_unique (:797) never sees the new claimant. Reproduced in review-probe-inplace.log: warm plans/alpha.html for slug alpha, rewrite plans/beta.html in place so it declares plan-slug alpha, and head resolves plans/alpha.html while base raises ResourceCollision 'duplicate resource sample:plan:alpha: plans/alpha.html, plans/beta.html'. That breaks the section's 'Every resolution returns what the base revision returns' and the docstring claim at :847 that only an entry set can hide behind the stamp; the fix is to key or invalidate the listing on the per-file signatures its consumers revalidate against, not only on the directory stamp.

_directory_stamp duplicates a capability the repository already owns: reckon/metadata_index.py:1394 _dir_identity returns the same directory entry-set identity, and reckon/file_memo.py:280 signature_from_stat is documented as the one place the five stat fields and their order are written; the diff writes the fields itself in a third order, and the same function already imports metadata_index at :865, so it duplicates rather than extends either owner.

The equality assertions at :146-:147 and :168 compare resolve_resource against resources.identify_resource, both in the module under test, and the test never rewrites a sibling in place, so the case where head differs from base (a refusal base made and head does not) is not reached and the gate stays green on the defect at reckon/resources.py:854; the repair owes a case that rewrites a sibling in place and asserts the refusal base gives.

The matched arms record tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py and tests/test_every_shared_home_lock_holds_across_nodes.py, neither of which imports reckon.resources, so the done_when's population ('the test files importing the changed modules', 17 files under tests/) was not the one measured and the arms say nothing about the changed module.
